title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_0RB0LF_1RA1RE_1RC---_1LC0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_0RB0LF_1RA1RE_1RC---_1LC0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. With a = 0001 and b = 001, at the left extensions the tape is C> b a^m b^x1 a b^x2 a ... a b^xk. The run lengths xi are mostly even and rise across the tape in plateaus of equal values with outliers (at step 5,543,681,176: 4, 2, 2, ..., 6 (11 times), 10 (5 times), 12, ..., 16, 18, 20, ..., up to above 120), and the width grows like 1.16·√t. The sweeps (which complement 001 ↔ 110 and similar words) are proved in Lean; the rule that updates the staircase is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,503 cells have been visited and 23,195 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.23). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text:
The head sweeps over long runs of a repeated word, rewriting each copy, for any number n of copies and any surrounding tape. Examples:
  • L D> (001)^n R → L (110)^n D> R
  • L A> (010)^n R → L (101)^n A> R
  • L B> (100)^n R → L (011)^n B> R
  • L 0 D> (1011011)^n R → L (1011011)^n 0 D> R
Generated by py/rules.py (tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: A staircase of runs
claims.text: At the 154 left extensions up to 6·109 steps (tools/c/tokrun, a = 0001, b = 001), the tape is C> b a^m b^x1 a b^x2 a ... a b^xk; the xi rise from about 4 at the left to about 120 at the right in plateaus of equal values, with a larger outlier at the end of most plateaus (e.g. 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 4 10 10 10 10 10 8 10 12 12 12 12 10 12 10 28 16 ...).

claims.title: Square-root width
claims.text: The width is 31,604 at step 7.39·10<sup>8</sup> and 86,428 at step 5.54·10<sup>9</sup>, about 1.16·√t.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.43×10<sup>9</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.43×109 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 4 checkpoints, the last at 109 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 58 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_0RC0LF_1LD0RE_1RC0LB_1RD1RA_1LB0LC up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_0LA0RE_1RD0RA_1LD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,503 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 10<sup>9</sup> steps).

sections.heading: A staircase of runs
html:
Write a for 0001 and b for 001. At the moments the head extends the tape to the left the tape is C> b a^m b^x1 a b^x2 a ... a b^xk: a short counter a^m and then runs of b separated by single as. Listing only the run lengths, at step 5,543,681,176:

4 2 2 . 2 4 2 4 2 16 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 4 10 10 10 10 10 8 10 12 12 12 12 10 12 10 28 16 16 16 16 16 20 18 ...

The lengths rise across the tape in plateaus, and the whole staircase shifts between sweeps (the same positions read 4 6 . 16 6 6 6 6 6 6 10 8 ... at step 2,666,118,079).

sections.heading: Sweeps
html: Each sweep runs over the whole tape complementing the words (D> (001)^n → (110)^n D>, A> (010)^n → (101)^n A>, ...: proved in Lean) and changes a few run lengths on the way. How it changes them, and so how the staircase evolves, is not known. A halt (E reading 1) has not occurred in 6·109 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.23). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,503 cells (558 left of the start, 26,367 right), with a density of 1s of 0.618.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC0LF_1LD0RE_1RC0LB_1RD1RA_1LB0LC: rename A→D, B→C, C→B, D→E, E→A, F→F; it is this table started in state E
  • 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_0LA0RE_1RD0RA_1LD---: rename A→B, B→A, C→D, D→C, E→F, F→E and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

summary: A long staircase of runs of 001 separated by 0001: the run lengths form a slowly rising sequence of plateaus (4, 6, ..., 120 across the tape), each sweep rewriting it; a small counter of 0001s sits at the left end. The width grows like the square root of the step count. Not understood; halting open.
